vopros: What's the best AI receptionist for a small business?

vyzhimka.tekst:
There's no single universal "best" — the right AI receptionist depends heavily on your call volume, industry, and whether you want AI-only or a human backup. That said, a few names show up consistently across independent tests and reviews, and I'll break down the top options by use case rather than name one winner (many "best AI receptionist" lists are published by the vendors themselves, so take #1 rankings with a grain of salt).

## By use case

**Home services / trades (plumbing, HVAC, electrical, roofing)**
Rosie is aimed squarely at small service businesses, and it trains itself on your website and Google Business Profile, answering calls in a natural voice within about an hour. A VC firm that tested nearly a dozen tools across its portfolio companies found Rosie was the best fit for most of their portfolio companies, from a single-location plumber to a 50+ location oil change franchise.

**Solo operators / very low call volume**
Goodcall is a flat-rate AI phone assistant with unlimited minutes for solopreneurs and micro-businesses. For basic call answering, if you just want calls answered well, Upfirst is the easiest to set up and fits most small businesses.

**Need occasional human backup (law firms, medical practices, high-stakes calls)**
Smith.ai combines AI call handling with a team of 500+ live human agents as backup and holds a 4.8/5.0 rating on Clutch with 100+ reviews — when the AI can't handle a call, it escalates to a human agent seamlessly, which works for businesses that want AI efficiency but need human warmth for complex situations. Note that human backup is often priced as a per-call add-on ($3 per handoff at Smith.ai, for example), not included in base plans.

**High call volume / predictable flat pricing**
Several newer entrants specifically target businesses that get burned by per-minute overages. For example, pure-AI platforms with full features run $199–299/month, with flat monthly pricing and unlimited calls so a busy month costs the same as a slow one — no per-minute charges or overage math.

**Multi-language / bilingual needs**
Some tools let you build a custom agent trained on your business in minutes with no code, answering on voice, SMS, WhatsApp, and web chat, in both English and Spanish. For broader language coverage, one option supports 74 languages.

**All-in-one front office (phone + CRM + scheduling)**
My AI Front Desk is an all-in-one AI front office bundle (phone, chat, SMS, CRM) for low-call-volume local businesses.

## Pricing landscape (roughly, as of 2026)

- **Budget/entry-level:** ~$25–49/month (Dialzara, Upfirst, Rosie, Voksha)
- **Mid-tier flat-rate:** ~$150–299/month for unlimited or high-volume plans
- **Hybrid AI+human:** ~$95–500+/month depending on human involvement
- **Traditional live answering service (for comparison):** $500–800/month for around 100 calls with overage charges on top, versus a human receptionist at $3,100–4,300/month all-in.

## What actually matters when choosing

Independent testers emphasize a few practical criteria over marketing claims: fast, clear setup (should be live within an hour) and a realistic voice — one reviewer called every tool from their own phone, and robotic or laggy voices didn't make the cut. Also worth checking: roughly 20% of AI-first calls still require human involvement, so how a service handles that handoff matters enormously.

**My practical suggestion:** Since most of these companies self-publish "best" rankings favoring themselves, don't trust any single article's #1 pick. Instead, shortlist 2–3 based on your specific need above (trades → Rosie; need human backup → Smith.ai; budget/simple → Upfirst or Dialzara; bilingual → Dapta), and use their free trials — call each one yourself with realistic scenarios (booking, FAQ, confused caller) before committing.
